newsitem.title: CANADA: Morrison CEO expects bid to be deemed low.
newsitem.headline: Morrison CEO expects bid to be deemed low.

text.p: Gordon Stollery, Chairman of takeover target Morrison Petroleums Ltd., said on Friday that newly hired advisers would likely deem Canadian 88 Energy Corp.'s hostile bid as too cheap.
"I'm going to wait to see what the investment guys say on Tuesday," Stollery said in an interview. "But I would be shocked if they didn't say something of that nature."
Stollery said the company's board of directors and fiancial advisers were slated to meet on Tuesday, then announce their recommendation to shareholders.

Calgary-based Canadian 88 plans to offer C$10 ($7.46) cash, up to a maximum of C$140 million ($104 million), or 1.5 of its shares for each share of larger Morrison, also of Calgary. The deal would be valued at C$652 million ($486 million).

Morrison, whose deep natural gas prospects in the foothills of southern Alberta are Canadian 88's main reason for pursuing the firm, said on Friday it hired brokerages Bunting Warburg Inc. and Nesbitt Burns Inc. as financial advisers. It also hired law firm Stikeman Elliott as legal adviser.

Stollery said Morrison was accelerating the release of financial statements and engineering reports in light of the offer. The data could reach shareholders "certainly within the first 21-day period and long before the 60 days of our shareholder rights plan," he said.

Canadian 88's offer is contingent on Morrison waiving the shareholder plan, or poison pill, which would add 39 days for considering the bid and allow shareholders to buy shares at half the market price.
However, further results from drilling at Morrison's much-watched Racehorse Creek foothills gas play would likely be announced over the next 30-40 days, he said.
Morrison reported disappointing results from the first phase of drilling on the prospect in December, which led to a steep decline in the company's stock price.

"We're looking at how we can (release the data sooner), but it's pretty difficult to expedite that high-tech type of activity in the foothills with expensive rigs and winter conditions," Stollery said.
Morrison shares in Toronto closed up C15 cents (11 cents) on Friday to C$10.50 ($7.83). Canadian 88 climbed C20 cents to C$6.60 ($4.92).
